podcast.body: The lead single from Bruno Mars's second album, "Unorthodox Jukebox," which heavily leaned into the influence of The Police and Sting, featuring lustful lyrics with a pre-chorus refrain "Your Sex Takes Me to Paradise" and a reggae-tinged, economical post-punk groove. It quickly rose to the top of the Hot 100 in December 2012 and held the position through January 2013 for six weeks, leading to an iconic Grammy performance where Sting himself joined Mars on stage. "Locked out of heaven was as lustful as Roxanne."

podcast.body: This 2012 number one smash by Bruno Mars was not a Sting sample or interpolation, but a deliberate "style imitation of The Police." Mars admitted in interviews that he was a huge Police fan and intended for "Locked Out of Heaven" to be his own Police-like track without directly sampling a specific song. It is a "deft similacrum" of The Police's blend of reggae and new wave, with Mars even doing an impression of Sting's falsetto vocals. Sting, though unpaid for the hit, endorsed it and performed the song with Mars at the 2013 Grammy Awards. "Mars has admitted in interviews he was a huge police fan and heaven was his attempt to write his own police track without jacking any specific song."
